title: The Saints and Sinners records: Dobell LP, Cav-A-Bob, and '150 years of jazz'
summary: He recalls a Toronto-made Saints and Sinners LP pressed in England with Buster Bailey, Vic Dickenson and himself billed as 150 years of jazz, with Rudy Powell and Eddie Barefield following Bailey.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I see. Uh-huh. Well then, when you went back in '69, how long did you stay that time? You stayed over there ten days in '68, you had ten dates here.
I think we did more than that, now, I'm trying to think what happened to me. I'll tell you right then that after that, I'm wondering, you know? I don't know right now. Anyway, --
Well you must have gone -- you talked of going to Stockholm, so you must have gone to Stockholm. The second time.
Yes. No, that was the first -- this time, on that trip, starting with the first, and from there we went back -- yeah, went to Germany, and did the recording date. We made the album, "Sugar."
Where did you make it?
At -- tuh, tuh, tuh, tuh, dah, it wouldn't be there. It's not --
No, it's not.
It's written on the record. I have the record over there. I can grab it in one minute and tell you.
Well you have a -- there's a Saints and Sinners record that was put out by Dobell, the English.
Yeah, well that's the -- I don't know.
That was another thing.
That's another one.
That's before.
Oh, that's before you were on the --
Yeah, I'm on there. Yes, I'm on it.
When was that made?
I think that's the thing we did in Toronto.
Oh, I see. I see. Done in Toronto, the same as the Cava-Bob ?
And they sent it over to be pressed. let me think now. Yeah. Or was that done here and sent over to England to be pressed? Because it had Buster Bailey on it. You remember Buster Bailey?
Oh yes, I remember --
Yeah, and what a band we had then. Buster Bailey, clarinet. Vic Dickenson, and Little Herman!
(Laughter.)

They used to write us up in the papers saying a 150 years of jazz, on the front line. More than a 150 years of jazz on the front line. Buster Bailey, Herman Autrey, and Vic Dickenson. And man, we used to have a lot of fun. My oh my. People used to come in and -- well, it was just nice.
Anyway, you know, very nice.
: Rudy Powell replaced Buster Bailey?
Yes.
: Followed him?

Yes, he followed Buster Bailey, uh-huh. Uh-huh. And I'm trying to think who else did we have. Well, Bushell not this -- uh, Eddie Barefield did a lot of those dates too. Know Eddie Barefield, clarinet player?
: Yeah, I know him, very fine.
